We'd had our puppy for about three weeks when I made the rookie mistake of leaving her alone for a couple hours.
I was fully convinced a tired puppy would just sleep the whole time, curled up peacefully like every other quiet afternoon.
I came home to find one couch cushion completely gutted.
Foam was scattered across the living room like it had snowed indoors, and my puppy sat proudly in the middle of it, looking extremely satisfied with herself.
That, it turned out, was just the opening act.
Tucked behind the couch was a chewed remote control, missing its back panel entirely, batteries rolled halfway across the room like tiny abandoned evidence.
I stood there in the doorway for a solid minute, just slowly turning in circles.
I was trying to take in the full scope of the damage before deciding where to even start cleaning any of it up.
I picked through the wreckage, trying to piece together exactly how much damage had happened in under two hours.
My puppy trotted over holding a single sock, clearly hoping I hadn't noticed that one yet.
I checked the rest of the apartment and found a shoe, thankfully just one.
It was chewed thoroughly enough that returning it to its matching pair felt like a genuinely lost cause, the sole barely hanging on anymore.
My roommate got home a little later and took one look at the living room.
She just started laughing and said she couldn't believe one small dog had managed this much chaos in such a short window.
She immediately grabbed her phone to take pictures, insisting the damage was too impressive not to document.
I just stood there holding a fistful of couch foam, not finding it quite as funny as she clearly did.

We spent that whole evening puppy-proofing everything within reach, moving cords, hiding shoes, and buying one of those ridiculously sturdy chew toys marketed as "indestructible." That felt like a personal challenge more than a product description.
The indestructible toy lasted, impressively, almost four full days before meeting a similar fate to the couch cushion.
At that point we just accepted defeat and bought a second one immediately, alongside a third one just in case, since apparently one indestructible toy was never actually going to be enough.
She's calmer now, mostly.
But we still never leave anything remotely chewable within reach, having learned the hard way that "she'll probably just sleep" is apparently the most optimistic sentence a new puppy owner can say.
Every new roommate who visits still gets shown that framed photo of the destroyed couch cushion, sitting proudly on our shelf now like some kind of trophy.
